title: Incident-Triggered Roadmap Rebalancer for Top Accounts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Major customers occasionally open urgent escalations (incidents, data/regulatory blockers, or performance regressions) that require rapid product work. Current intake is ad hoc: PMs triage through Slack/Zoom, engineering triages through on-call channels, and roadmap commits happen informally. This causes unclear expectations, churn across cycles, and misaligned prioritization with other customers.

Goal: Define a repeatable, auditable 'Incident-Triggered Roadmap Rebalancer' process for top accounts that: 1) automatically evaluates whether an escalation should surface into near-term roadmap re-prioritization, 2) provides structured trade-off guidance to PM/Eng/CS leadership, and 3) documents customer-visible commitments and fallback behavior.

Scope: This ticket covers the PM-side policy, decision matrix, communication templates, measurement plan, and a lightweight automation to turn an incident signal into a formal Rebalance Review. Engineering work to build automation hooks (alert -> ticket creation) will be captured as ENG dependencies.

High-level approach:
- Define trigger taxonomy (incident severity + customer tier + SLA exposure + revenue/account health) that maps to one of: Advisory (no roadmap change), Fast-Track (pull into next sprint), Hotfix (patch ASAP, out-of-band), or Escalation Escrow (deferred but contractual runway).
- Create decision matrix with explicit criteria and example scenarios to reduce ad-hoc judgments.
- Create a Rebalance Review template (Confluence) and a Rebalance Ticket template (Linear) with required artifacts: incident timeline, impact quantification, proposed scope (MVP vs. comprehensive), estimated effort, rollback/fallback options, customer communication draft, and acceptance criteria.
- Define SLA-aligned commitment ladders and guardrails (e.g., maximum N sprint swaps per quarter per account, deferral credits).
- Integrate with CS/Support playbook: who owns customer communication, what language to use, and cadence for status updates.
- Build lightweight automation (ENG) to create a PM Rebalance ticket when incident meets trigger rules and to notify stakeholders in #top-account-ops channel.
- Define KPIs: mean time-to-decision (hours), % of Rebalance Reviews that result in roadmap changes, customer satisfaction delta post-resolution, and number of sprint swaps per quarter.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision matrix documented and validated by 3 PMs, 2 Eng leads, and Head of CS.
- Rebalance Review Confluence template published with at least 2 example case studies from past incidents.
- Linear ticket template created and productized (aligned with agents.md metadata).
- Automation spec drafted and ENG dependency created (ENG-2021).
- Communication templates for customer-facing commit and apology language approved by Legal and CS.
- Pilot execution plan for 3 flagship accounts and success metrics defined.

Out of scope: Permanent major roadmap reshuffles driven by product strategy (these remain quarterly planning decisions). This playbook handles urgent, customer-impacting escalations where near-term product change is plausible.
